name: A failed statement must be observationally removable

payload.description: Within an explicit transaction, removing a failed statement must not change the later committed row, index, constraint, or terminal state.
payload.candidate_shape: A successful statement first mutates owner set A; a later statement revisits A plus new owners, performs partial work, then fails and rolls back.
admission_gates: the second statement must fail before transaction commit
the failure must occur after at least one row/index owner was visited
the control executes the same transaction without the failed statement
fresh durable state and every affected index must equal the control
payload.negative_screen: A MemDB flag or checkpoint omission is not executable evidence until a TiDB production setter reaches a correctness-bearing consumer.

provenance.source: failed-statement owner-revisit matrix on TiDB master

steps: create identical control and probe tables with primary, unique, ordinary, and generated indexes
begin the same optimistic or pessimistic explicit transaction
execute successful mutation A on both
only on probe execute mutation B that revisits A, changes at least one owner, then fails on a deterministic row-local error
compare exact fresh rowsets, ADMIN CHECK, and forced record/index scans
required_witnesses: B returns an error before COMMIT
B's SQL ordering reaches an earlier valid row before the failing row
control and probe use the same transaction mode and initial state
invalid_triggers: duplicate conflict discovered only at COMMIT in optimistic mode
a declared CHECK constraint that is not enforced in the runtime
an error before any mutation owner is visited

payload.red: After B errors and the transaction commits, probe differs from control in base rows, any unique/ordinary/generated index scan, ADMIN CHECK, or terminal result.
payload.green: For every matrix cell, probe equals control in exact base rows; ADMIN CHECK succeeds; every forced index scan equals the record scan.
blind_to: session-local effects intentionally defined to survive statement failure
failures that occur only during COMMIT
unreachable client-go flags without a TiDB setter

name: Failed row and index owner rewrites are removed at statement rollback

payload.source_shape: MemDB key flags are not all checkpointed as ordinary values, suggesting that a failed statement might poison a prior mutation.
payload.reachability_screen: NewlyInserted could theoretically suppress a tombstone delete, but current TiDB production code does not set the client-go flag; test-only setters are not candidate ingress.

owner_shapes: delete then failed insert with new owner
update then failed update after index rewrite
executed_matrix.failure: NOT NULL violation after an earlier row owner is revisited

payload.observed: All 10 cells matched the transaction with the failed statement removed; base, unique, ordinary, and generated indexes remained consistent.
payload.reopen_only_if: a current TiDB setter reaches a surviving non-value MemDB flag whose highest consumer changes the final mutation set or assertion semantics

name: Failed owner-revisiting statement must be removable before transaction commit

payload.p_check: Statement rollback restores the MemDB staging checkpoint after B has revisited row and index owners touched by A.
payload.q_claim: No B-owned value, flag, assertion, or mutation classification can affect the later transaction commit.
payload.f_effect: A surviving side state could suppress a required delete/put or leave a row-index mismatch after COMMIT.
payload.result: GREEN across 10 real-TiKV cells; no reachable surviving correctness-bearing owner found.

title: Failed statement might poison a prior mutation through non-value MemDB state

payload.do_not_repeat: Do not enumerate SQL shapes. Reopen only with a production-reachable setter and a named surviving consumer.

rationale: The control removes exactly the failed statement while preserving transaction history and mode.
Durable equality must include every physical index owner, not only table rows.
Current reachable owner-revisit shapes are protected; source-only flags without production setters are rejected.

evidence.observed: The duplicate conflict was deferred until COMMIT, so no failed statement rollback occurred.

lessons.trigger_gate: An error expected from a statement is invalid if optimistic constraint checking delays it to transaction commit.

evidence.observed: The CHECK predicate did not produce an error in the runtime, so the probe never entered statement rollback.

lessons.trigger_gate: A declared constraint is not a fault producer until runtime enforcement is proved.

evidence.oracle: exact control/probe rows equal; ADMIN CHECK passed; u1/u2/base/generated forced scans equal record scan

lessons.guard: Reachable row/index side effects were removed by statement checkpoint rollback.
lessons.selector_refinement: Require a production setter and highest consumer before spending runtime on a non-value MemDB flag.
lessons.harness_lesson: NOT NULL after an earlier valid row gives a deterministic statement-local failure in both transaction modes.
